design.objective: Show directly related historical applications and their current statuses inside additional-application details for approval reference.
users: Approvers and authorized release-application viewers reviewing an additional application

requirements.statement: Only additional applications must expose a related-history section sourced from persisted ADDITIONAL relations.
acceptance: Additional details load direct related history
Standard applications do not show the section
Later or unrelated same-window applications are not included
requirements.source: User selected directly related historical applications on 2026-08-20.
counterexample: The section uses the dynamic conflict list

requirements.statement: Each related application must show its code, current status, version type, requester, department, creation time, release time, requirements and description.
acceptance: All listed fields are visible without leaving the current approval detail
Status reflects the current historical-application state
counterexample: Only an application code is shown
Status is a stale relation snapshot

requirements.statement: Related delivery and file-media changes must be recomputed from current active items and grouped by historical application.
acceptance: Multiple relation rows produce one application entry
Removed current items do not appear
Displayed before/after values match current active content
requirements.source: Existing revision-preserving data model and confirmed design.
counterexample: A historical application is duplicated per delivery row
A removed draft item remains in the reference list

requirements.statement: Related applications must be sorted by latest release time and link to their in-app details without embedding attachments.
acceptance: Application code opens its detail route
No attachment payload is returned by the history endpoint
counterexample: The reference endpoint duplicates attachment data

requirements.statement: The endpoint must enforce tenant isolation and release-application view permission without broad fallback queries.
acceptance: The endpoint requires release:application:view or system:admin
Empty relations return an empty list
counterexample: A missing relation triggers a same-window scan
A user without view permission can query history

requirements.statement: Related-history empty and error states must remain local and must not block the main detail or approval panel.
acceptance: Empty additional history has explicit copy
A history request failure exposes local retry
Main detail and approval controls remain available
counterexample: History failure causes the whole detail page to fail
An empty section silently disappears on an additional application

invariants: rel_application_relation remains the lineage fact source
Existing approval and conflict behavior is unchanged
constraints: Reuse Spring JDBC and existing release module patterns
Do not add a database migration
Remain on rokey and add no dependency
non_goals: Modify historical applications from the reference area

selected_approach.name: Persisted relation aggregation through a dedicated read endpoint
selected_approach.reason: It provides exact lineage semantics, avoids recursive DTO expansion and prevents later or unrelated same-window applications from appearing.

alternatives.name: Reuse dynamic conflict report
alternatives.rejected_because: It can include applications created after the current application and is not immutable lineage.

alternatives.name: List every earlier application in the same window and subsystem
alternatives.rejected_because: It adds noise and does not identify the applications that directly caused additional classification.

components.name: ReleaseApplicationStore
components.responsibility: Return direct historical application IDs for active ADDITIONAL relation items within the tenant.

components.name: ReleaseApplicationService
components.responsibility: Authorize the current application, aggregate related applications, recompute changes and sort the read model.
depends_on: Existing application loaders and item-change logic

components.name: ReleaseApplicationController
components.responsibility: Expose the permission-protected related-history read endpoint.

components.name: Release API client
components.responsibility: Define the flat history contract and fetch related history.

components.name: ReleaseApplicationDetailPage
components.responsibility: Load history independently and render additional-only reference, empty, error and link states.

interfaces.name: GET /api/release/applications/{code}/related-history
interfaces.contract: Returns a tenant-scoped flat list of directly related historical applications with current status and recomputed changes; never includes attachments or conflict actions.

data_flows.input: Current application code and authenticated user
transitions: resolve persisted ADDITIONAL relation IDs matching active items
data_flows.output: Flat related-history list for approval reference

error_handling.condition: Current application is missing or cross-tenant
error_handling.behavior: Use existing not-found or forbidden semantics.
error_handling.recovery: User returns to the authorized application list.

error_handling.condition: A relation points to a deleted or unavailable historical application
error_handling.behavior: Skip that relation while retaining other valid history.
error_handling.recovery: Data repair can restore the missing business record without endpoint changes.

error_handling.behavior: Keep main detail and approval usable and show a local retry state.

error_handling.condition: Additional application has no valid related history
error_handling.behavior: Show an explicit empty state and do not broaden the query.
error_handling.recovery: Correct relation data through the normal application flow or data repair.

performance: Relation-index lookup and bounded related ID set
compatibility: No schema or existing DTO changes required
operations: Local endpoint failure is observable in the detail section

verification_strategy.signal: Store and service return only direct, active, tenant-scoped grouped history.
verification_strategy.method: Focused persistence and service tests with later, unrelated, stale and cross-tenant fixtures.

verification_strategy.signal: The API exposes complete summary fields, live status, recomputed changes and stable ordering.
The detail page shows additional-only reference cards, working links and isolated empty/error states.
verification_strategy.method: Frontend build and authenticated browser checks.

verification_strategy.signal: Release module and frontend regressions remain green.
verification_strategy.method: Maven release-module tests, npm production build and git diff check.

assumptions.text: Persisted ADDITIONAL relations exist for formally created additional applications and active-item filtering removes stale revision rows.
assumptions.basis: Current create/update service calls persistAdditionalRelations and delivery revisions preserve active flags.
assumptions.falsifier: Fixtures show valid additional applications without any persisted relations or current active item keys.

unknowns.question: Should a logically deleted historical source remain as an immutable non-clickable audit snapshot?
unknowns.impact: Current design skips unavailable sources; a future audit requirement may need snapshot persistence.

decisions.decision: Display only directly related historical applications.
decisions.reason: This is the scope explicitly selected by the user.

decisions.decision: Expose a dedicated flat read endpoint.
decisions.reason: It avoids recursive Response growth and keeps list/conflict payloads unchanged.

decisions.decision: Read status live and recompute changes from active content.
decisions.reason: This prevents stale relation snapshots after draft revisions.
The reference remains scannable and links to the full historical detail when needed.

risks.risk: Legacy or stale relation rows refer to items no longer active.
risks.mitigation: Join/filter against current active delivery item keys and recompute changes.

risks.risk: Multiple relation rows duplicate a historical application.
risks.impact: The page becomes noisy and counts are misleading.
risks.mitigation: Deduplicate IDs in persistence and aggregate changes per historical application in the service.

risks.risk: Independent history loading can create a brief layout shift.
risks.impact: Approval page may move after initial render.
risks.mitigation: Use a stable local loading state with bounded minimum height.

approval.evidence: The user selected directly related historical applications and confirmed the proposed backend and detail-page design on 2026-08-20.

global_constraints: Remain on rokey and preserve unrelated dirty-worktree changes
No database migration, dependency, attachment expansion or approval-write change
Use independently recoverable frontend history state
